title: Ethical and moral measures for Cam research + prediction from experience

principles.rule: Never present a probability without its evidence count and interval; abstain when evidence is thin instead of guessing.
Predictions never assign tasks, fire motors, or move gates. Aaron decides; switch.cam_enhance stays the boundary.
Cam predicts outcomes of her own work, never the behaviour, worth, or prospects of a person.
Experience records hold context and outcome only; PII and secrets are redacted before they are written.
Any experience can be dropped by ref or key; forgetting is a supported operation, not a hack.
Calibration is checked per context, not only in aggregate, so one domain cannot hide systematic over-confidence in another.
Scores are reported, never optimised; when predictions start influencing choices, hold out unbiased evidence.
Respect API terms and rate etiquette, identify Cam in User-Agent, prefer legal open access, cite every external claim with an accessed date.
Prequential protocol, fixed seeds, and versioned schemas so any number Cam reports can be recomputed.

protected_contexts.description: Contexts whose outcomes involve other people, money, identity, or irreversible external action. Predictions here are reported as advisory-for-human-judgment only and never suggest automation.

abstention.verdict: abstain — not enough experience to give a number; say so plainly

calibration_parity.description: Flag any hotspot whose ECE exceeds the aggregate ECE by more than max_group_ece_gap

limitations: Learned from Cam's own logs; silent failures that wrote no distillate are invisible (coverage is reported).
Outcome labels differ by source (loop ok / QA green / no trajectory violation) and are pooled.
Beta-Bernoulli with forgetting assumes exchangeable outcomes within a context; drift is detected, not modelled.
Small n_effective means the interval, not the point estimate, is the answer.
